title: Speaking Part 1 — react, answer, expand
note:
The ladder is the default's formula: react, answer, then expand with a reason, an example and a contrast. It is not new to this repo — part1-structure.json's phraseBank already holds it as five steps, and this file is that bank turned into something a student does rather than reads.

THE REACTION IS PREPENDED. Level 1 is the bare answer a student gives unprompted; round 1 puts a reaction in FRONT of it. The screen performs the rule, which is the one thing a phrase list cannot do. Every other move is appended.

Every level is written in full by a person. The engine never composes an answer — it only chooses which level to show. Three voices run the same ladder at the same depth, so switching changes whose life it is, not how developed the answer is.

icon and color are deliberately absent. The old bank stored an emoji and a hex per step, and presentation inside a data file is how a page ends up carrying five saturated hues from no palette in this product.

x.name: React
x.hint: how you feel about the question, before you answer it

e.name: Example
e.hint: one specific thing from your own life

c.name: Contrast
c.hint: the other side, so the answer sounds balanced

phraseBank.heading: Reacting — not keen
phrases: I can't say I'm keen on…
I've never been that bothered about…
I'd rather not, if I'm honest…

phraseBank.heading: Reacting — fronted, and worth two criteria
phraseBank.note: These are clefts. They mark the discourse and count as complex structures at the same time.
phrases: The thing I love about… is…
If there's one thing I…, it's…

tip: Don't memorise answers. Start with your reaction, develop the idea, add an example, show some balance. An answer that follows the shape sounds natural; an answer that recites it does not.
